summary: Iteration 2 tested the v2 enhancements on backend and frontend. Backend: 11/11 pytest tests passed (tests/test_v2_campaigns.py, which uses the LIVE worker) and 27/27 in-process checks passed (tests/inprocess_mailer_check.py). Verified: catalogue v2 (exactly 4 packages with correct prices and monthly fees; 9 old services archived); sender identity and IMAP settings (the password is never returned); saving IMAP security; Visabal brief (all sections present, 400 when unassessed, 404 when unknown); creating a campaign with draft_ids [] and a daily_limit; PATCH daily_limit validation (1-500, 404 when unknown); the mode API (autonomous without confirm returns 400); the live worker Review Mode flow (outbound kind initial, followup_status scheduled, due about 5 business days later); per-campaign daily limit 1 enforced, with waiting_reason 'campaign daily limit reached (1/1)'; the follow-up worker (a 'Re: ...' pending_approval draft, then approve, then sent as kind followup, parent status 'sent', only one follow-up); pausing or stopping cancels scheduled follow-ups; campaign analytics fields; Full Autonomy auto-enrolment (approved_by full_autonomy, then sent); unsubscribe on a non-test outbound cancels follow-ups and suppresses the address; duplicate guard ('this address has already been emailed'); email.opened recorded and does not cancel the follow-up; the autonomy follow-up is auto-approved and sent with In-Reply-To/References equal to the original Message-ID, reply_to support@, ABN in the footer, no GST; handle_reply (replied, follow-ups cancelled, sentiment 'positive', urgent notification); IMAP poll with a monkeypatched fetch (matched_by message_id, recorded once, business replied, follow-ups cancelled, sentiment set); bounce and complaint webhooks (cancel follow-ups and suppress); bounce_guard auto-pause; Melbourne resolve reuses the region (created False, no new region, 94 butchers zones completed). Frontend: Service Catalogue (4 cards), Visabal tab with Copy brief (toast shown), green REPLIED row in Prospects, New campaign form with daily limit, mode toggle (browser confirm, then label and API update, then back to review), per-campaign daily limit save, IMAP SSL/TLS select (ssl/starttls/none; Save mailbox works), regression pages (dashboard, live, coverage with 262 circles, assessments, replies, notifications, all 7 settings tabs, new search), and mobile at 390px with no horizontal overflow on /, /live and /campaigns. No page errors.

minor.issue: The review request said there was no Resend key, but GET /api/settings shows resend.api_key_set=true (hint …Czqx) and imap.password_set=true (…0KC!). So test-mode sends really go through Resend to delivered@resend.dev with status 'sent', not 'test_dry_run'. About 5 TEST emails were sent to delivered@resend.dev during the live-worker tests. The dry-run path was verified in-process with the key blanked. Also, sending.test_mode was FALSE when testing started (audit shows it was toggled at 02:56). The tester set it to true and left it true.

sent_today uses UTC midnight and does not filter on test_mode, while worker.sender_step enforces the per-campaign daily limit from Australia/Melbourne midnight with the current test_mode. The UI '(x/N today)' can disagree with the limit actually enforced. Use the same Melbourne-day calculation.

sort=[('kind', -1), ...] puts 'initial' before 'followup' (descending alphabetical), so follow-ups are de-prioritised behind new initial emails. Legacy drafts with no kind field sort last. If follow-ups were meant to go first, use an explicit priority field.

When sent_count reaches the campaign limit, the campaign is marked 'completed' without cancel_followups. Its scheduled follow-ups stay 'scheduled' forever: followup_step only runs for running campaigns, and the analytics keep counting them as scheduled. Either cancel them or keep processing follow-ups for completed campaigns.

An autonomous campaign with no search_ids enrolls ANY pending_approval draft in the DB with campaign_id None, i.e. every real prospect. This is by design but risky. Real data currently has two businesses ('Hagen's Organic Butcher' and 'Hagen's') with pending drafts to the same address heybutcher@hagensorganics.com.au. The duplicate guard blocks the second at send time, but consider deduplicating by recipient when drafts are generated or approved.

The bakeries Melbourne test search (3 zones, max 2) was created and reused the existing region. However, the Overpass mirror maps.mail.ru returned mostly 504 errors, so zones_done stayed at 0 (zone_errors 1) over about 10 min, and butchers stayed at 94/262. Round-robin between searches is working (it alternated Brighton and Melbourne). Business de-duplication for the new category could not be verified. 'Niddrie completed: 0 found' happened during the degradation; check whether an empty or remark response is being treated as a real 0 result.

issues: Selecting STARTTLS silently changes the port to 143, and it is saved with the security setting. This is acceptable, but it is easy to miss. The tester restored ssl/993 via the API.
Shows '- Discovery source: None' when source_url is missing; show 'n/a' instead

Native <select> elements are still used (filters, drafts filter, IMAP security). Content on Campaigns/Services/Integrations is capped at about 1080px on 1920px screens (carried over from iteration 1).

action_items: Align GET /api/campaigns sent_today with the worker's Melbourne-day and test_mode logic
Cancel (or keep processing) scheduled follow-ups when a campaign auto-completes because it reached its limit
Decide on follow-up vs initial priority in sender_step ordering (currently initial first)
Deduplicate drafts that share a recipient (e.g. the two Hagen's records) before approval or autonomy enrolment
Note: a Resend key and an IMAP password ARE configured, and test_mode was off at the start of testing; confirm this is intended
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is still about 1187 lines; split it into routers
list_campaigns has N+1 queries and loads all outbound documents twice per campaign; aggregate instead
The mode confirm flag is only a client-sent boolean (fine for a single admin, but it is not a real second factor)
Webhook duplicate detection still catches every Exception from insert_one (iteration 1 comment)

success_rate.backend: 100% (11/11 pytest + 27/27 in-process); geographic de-duplication for the new category is unverified because of the Overpass outage

Real drafts are unchanged (8 pending_approval, 2 approved). Left in place: the 'bakeries' Melbourne search (id 0f7b5d51..., 3 zones, max 2), which is running as the brief requested. Final state: test_mode true, sending 9-17, weekdays_only true, interval 180, daily_limit 30, IMAP ssl/993 (password untouched, enabled false), agent running, Melbourne butchers search running.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend/tests && python -m pytest test_v2_campaigns.py -n0 -v (needs Melbourne local time within the temporarily opened 0-24 hours; it sets and restores sending settings; with the Resend key present, sends go to delivered@resend.dev). In-process logic: cd /app/backend && /root/.venv/bin/python tests/inprocess_mailer_check.py (no real sends; monkeypatches httpx and the IMAP fetch). Editing files under /app/backend triggers a uvicorn reload, which restarts the worker. Unverified: whether the bakeries search de-duplicates existing businesses (Overpass was down).
